info.title: Squally Read API
info.description:
Read access to a Squally organization's test results, for scripts, CI jobs and AI agents.

**Authentication.** Every request goes to `https://app.squally.dev/api/v1` plus the path and carries an organization read key as `Authorization: Bearer sqly_ro_…`. With the key in `SQUALLY_API_KEY` - the variable the MCP server reads too - the first request lists the organization's projects:
```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SQUALLY_API_KEY" https://app.squally.dev/api/v1/projects
```
A read key is organization-wide (every project), created by an organization admin in Organization › Read keys, and expires after 30, 60, 90, 180 days as chosen at creation. There is no renewal: create a new key and revoke the old one. Project ingest keys (`sqly_…`) are refused with `wrong_key_type`.

**Expiry warning.** From 7 days before a key expires, every authenticated response carries `Squally-Key-Expires-At` with the expiry instant (ISO-8601). Once it has passed, every request with the key is answered 401 `key_expired` ("This read key expired on <date>. Create a new one in Organization › Read keys."); an expired key is never extended. To rotate without a gap: create a new key, switch your callers to it, then revoke the old one - an organization may hold several active keys, and each works until it expires or is revoked.

**Rate limit.** Currently 60 requests per 60 seconds per key - a read key has its own budget, shared with nothing else. Over the limit the API answers 429 with `Retry-After: 60` and the usual error body, `{"error": "Too many requests with this read key. Wait 60 seconds, then retry.", "code": "rate_limited"}`. A caller far beyond the limit can be stopped earlier by the edge firewall with a bare 429 - no body, no `Retry-After`: wait 60 seconds just the same.

**Counts.** A run's `total`, `passed`, `failed`, `flaky` and `skipped` count tests, each test once over all the run's shards by its final attempt: `passed` on the first try, `flaky` after a retry, `failed` when the final attempt failed; `total` = `passed` + `failed` + `skipped` + `flaky`. Figures over a period - a test's runs, an error's occurrences - count finished runs of the `source` parameter's kind, as each field's description says.

**Playwright projects.** A run counts like Playwright: one row and one count per project's variant of a test - the run routes. Anything collected across runs counts a test ONCE across its Playwright projects and names them - `/tests`, a test's metrics and history, `/errors`, `/overview`: a run failed for the test when it failed in any project, flaky when it passed only after a retry in some project and failed in none. Since 1.0.0-beta.19; each project's variant was its own test before.

**Run numbers.** `runNumber` is the run's number in its project, the #12 the app shows: counted up from 1 per project, one number for all shards of a run, never given twice. Runs removed by the plan's retention leave gaps. The run routes take the run's `id`, not its number.

**Paging.** `/projects` and `/projects/{projectId}/branches` answer with every item at once, no paging. `/runs` pages with a cursor (`cursor`, `direction`, `perPage`); `/tests` and `/errors` page by number (`page`, 1-based - a page past the end answers the last page - and `perPage`).

**Retries.** 429: wait the seconds Retry-After names (60), then retry. Requests are counted per key in 60-second windows. 5xx: retry with exponential backoff, starting at 1 second and capped at 30 seconds. 400, 401, 403, 404: never retry - the same request gets the same answer.

**Plans.** The read API is part of the Standard and Pro plans. A key of an organization on Free is answered 403 `tier_too_low`; keys are not revoked on a downgrade and work again after an upgrade.

**Errors.** Every error is `{"error": "<sentence>", "code": "<slug>"}`. The sentence may be reworded; the slug may not. An id that does not exist and an id that belongs to another organization get the same 404, byte for byte.

**Test names in paths.** Test names are Playwright title paths and often contain `/`: URL-encode them, including `/` as `%2F`. The /tests/{testName} routes take a test's name without its project, as /tests lists it; a run's attempts route takes the name the run lists, with its project.

**Sharded runs** are returned as one logical run: /runs lists one row per logical run, and the run routes answer for all shards whichever shard's id you pass.

**Stability.** v1, beta. The API may change until the beta ends; every change is listed in the changelog (docs/openapi/CHANGELOG.md).

get.description: Runs in a period, newest first - one row per logical run (a sharded CI run is one row; each job of a CI run that sets a job key is its own run, see jobKey), placed in the period and ordered by the start of its first shard (since 1.0.0-beta.13). get.description: Every test with a run of the source (all by default) in the period and its metrics - stability, flaky rate, failure rate, runs, time lost, its median duration, its last 20 runs, the branches it ran on and where it fails most - ranked by the chosen sort. Each test once across its Playwright projects, its projects named and each project's own numbers in variants (since 1.0.0-beta.19; one item per project before). Counts finished runs of the source - all by default - without mass-failure runs, on every branch unless branch names one (see population). Moderate: aggregate queries over the period's results of the source, paged in the database; use the metrics route for one test.

parameters.description: The period, in days, ending now. Must not exceed the plan's retention (Standard 60, Pro 90 days); a longer period is refused with 400 invalid_period rather than answered with less data.

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Only runs on this branch, the name exactly. Every branch when absent.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Which runs count, by where they ran: all - every run (the default since 1.0.0-beta.18; ci before); ci - runs a shard reported a CI provider for; local - runs no shard did. The response's population names the one counted.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Only these Playwright projects, exactly (e.g. chromium) - repeat the parameter for several: ?project=chromium&project=firefox. Each test then counts only those projects' variants. Every project when absent. Called browser, one value, until 1.0.0-beta.19 - browser is now a 400.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Ranking, the worst first: stability (the default) lowest first; flakyRate, failureRate, runs and timeLost highest first. Ties go to the most runs (for runs: the lowest stability), then to the test name and file. A rate with nothing to divide by (null) sorts after every number.
